slides.heading: Majority Element
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Majority Element, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: An element occurs in more than half the array; find it (Boyer-Moore voting).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. An element occurs in more than half the array; find it (Boyer-Moore voting).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Boyer-Moore voting: pair off different values; the majority survives the cancellation.
slides.narration: Boyer-Moore voting: pair off different values; the majority survives the cancellation.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: count each value → O(n²)
Hash map counts → O(n) time, O(n) space
Sort and take the middle → O(n log n)
Boyer–Moore voting → O(n) time, O(1) space
slides.narration: Counting each value separately is quadratic. A hash map is linear but uses memory, and sorting puts the majority in the middle in n log n. Boyer-Moore voting gets linear time with constant space, by letting different values cancel each other out.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Keep a candidate and a count
3. When the count hits zero, adopt the current value
4. The final candidate is the answer
slides.narration: Step by step. First, keep a candidate and a count. Second, same value increments, different decrements. Third, when the count hits zero, adopt the current value. Fourth, the final candidate is the answer.

slides.narration: Element 1 matches the candidate, so the count goes up. Candidate 1, count 1.

slides.narration: Element 2 differs from the candidate, so it cancels one vote. Candidate 1, count 0.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We keep a candidate and a count. When the count is zero, the current value becomes the candidate. Then the count goes up for a match and down otherwise. The final candidate is returned.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Guaranteed majority exists here; otherwise verify with a 2nd pass
Count resets don't lose the answer
slides.narration: This problem guarantees a majority exists. Without that guarantee, you'd need a second pass to verify the candidate.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: elements appearing > n/3 times (two candidates)
slides.narration: Explain the intuition: the majority has more votes than everything else combined, so it survives the cancellations. The follow-up finds elements appearing more than n over three times with two candidates.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Boyer-Moore voting: pair off different values; the majority survives the cancellation.
slides.narration: To recap Majority Element: Boyer-Moore voting: pair off different values; the majority survives the cancellation. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
